newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel trades at record volumes.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel trades at record volumes.

text.p: Singapore gas oil traded at yet another one-day record when 2.44 million barrels exchanged hands, involving the same three trading firms as buyers, traders said.

They said that despite the huge volumes, in which 16 cargoes were involved, prices fell by between 40 and 80 cents per barrel from Wednesday's deals. First half May cargoes were traded between $26.50 and $26.60 per barrel while second half May cargoes were done between $25.70 and $26.45 free-on-board (fob) basis.

Traders said the lower prices reflected the large volumes of cargoes on sale. The sellers were a European major with six cargoes, a Swiss trader with four cargoes, another European major, a Malaysian trader, a Japanese trader and a US trader with one cargo each.
Traders said the three trading firms have among them bought at least a whopping 17 million barrels since March 3.
They said arbitrage cargoes continued to be fixed to Asia with the latest supply source from the U.S. Gulf Coast.

Traders said one of the Singapore traders recently sold a gas oil cargo to a Chinese buyer at $1.30.$1.35 per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, cost-and-freight southern China. The price is higher than current bids from Hong Kong seen at $1.10 per barrel premiums, c-and-f.
Traders also said there have been other scattered purchases from China one of which were around 20 cents per barrel over Singapore spot quotes fob South Korea basis.
Traders said one of the Singapore traders also bought 100,000 barrels of jet fuel from a US trader at $24.25 per barrel for May 9-13 lifting fob, about 35 cents below the deal on Wednesday.
Sri Lanka would decide on Friday on issuing a diesel and jet fuel tender for mid-day delivery to Colombo, a source said.
